Nilpena Ediacara National Park, which includes the former Ediacara Conservation Park, is a national park located in the northern Flinders Ranges, in the state of South Australia. It is significant for its abundance of Ediacaran fossils, so named because of their discovery in the Ediacara Hills. It is located about around 551 km (342 mi) north of the city of Adelaide, around 30 kilometres (19 miles) south-west of the town of Leigh Creek in the state's Far North, and lies on the traditional lands of the Adnyamathanha people.
The Flinders Ranges Ediacara Foundation was established in 2018 with a charter to protect the unique fossils.  The park, which includes the Ediacara Hills and covers 60,617 hectares (149,790 acres), was proclaimed in June 2021, and opened in April 2023. The park and the fossils are of major significance to the bid for UNESCO World Heritage Listing for the Flinders Ranges.


== Etymology ==
The name "Ediacara" has a disputed origin from one of the Aboriginal languages near the Flinders Range area. It is first known to have been used during the middle of the 19th century. Earlier Australian sources suggested that the "name 'Ediacara' or 'Idiyakra' may be derived from...

Select a tab About See and do Safety Fees Maps Locat­ed on the tra­di­tion­al lands of the Adnya­math­anha peo­ple, Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park (over 90,000 hectares) offers a tru­ly unique expe­ri­ence, pro­vid­ing vis­i­tors access to an ancient, fos­silised seafloor where ani­mal life first emerged more than 550 mil­lion years ago. There is no inde­pen­dent access to the park, vis­i­ta­tion is through small, guide-led tours only (the fos­sil sites are frag­ile, and the fos­sil field is a work­ing research site). The Edi­acara Expe­ri­ence Tour (two-hour tour) and the Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour (three-hour tour) leave from the entrance to the park using a wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus and book­ing well in advance is recommended. Both tours include the Nilpe­na Wool­shed and the Blacksmith’s Shop locat­ed in the main Vis­i­tor Precinct with the Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour trav­el­ling out to the near­by Fos­sil Field. Vis­i­tors will expe­ri­ence an area rich in cul­tur­al her­itage, pas­toral his­to­ry (for­mer­ly Nilpe­na Sta­tion) and flo­ra and fau­na includ­ing sig­nif­i­cant bio­di­ver­si­ty and threat­ened eco­log­i­cal communities. Be pre­pared for some­thing com­plete­ly different…The Blacksmith’s Shop offers an immer­sive, high-tech inter­pre­ta­tive pro­jec­tion of what ear­ly ani­mal life might have looked like mapped onto the nine metre Alice’s Restau­rant Bed , a com­plex fos­sil bed trans­port­ed piece by piece from a near­by hill­side to the Vis­i­tor Precinct. For those join­ing the Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour bring a sense of adven­ture and dis­cov­ery – you’ll be walk­ing around an active pale­on­to­log­i­cal research site where you can see fos­sil beds left in their orig­i­nal location. The Edi­acara fos­sils are inter­na­tion­al­ly sig­nif­i­cant because they pro­vide the ear­li­est known evi­dence of com­plex ani­mal life on Earth. Unlike most fos­sil sites, Nilpe­na pre­serves entire com­mu­ni­ties of soft-bod­ied organ­isms exact­ly as they lived on an ancient seabed, allow­ing sci­en­tists to study the struc­ture and func­tion of one of the world’s first ecosys­tems. Research at the site has revealed the ear­li­est evi­dence of ani­mal move­ment, repro­duc­tion, scav­eng­ing behav­iour and com­plex eco­log­i­cal inter­ac­tions, fun­da­men­tal­ly chang­ing our under­stand­ing of how life evolved on Earth. Gain­ing the atten­tion of world acclaimed con­ser­va­tion­ist Sir David Atten­bor­ough and Nation­al Aero­nau­tics and Space Admin­is­tra­tion ( NASA ) , Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is pro­vid­ing insight into a lit­tle-known age long before dinosaurs, megafau­na, or human habi­ta­tion – the Edi­acaran Period. World Her­itage list­ing is being pur­sued for sev­en sites in the Flinders Ranges (includ­ing Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park) with the final deci­sion expect­ed mid-2027. Annu­al sum­mer closure Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is closed from 1 Decem­ber to 15 March each year due to extreme sum­mer heat and fire risk. Tour Details Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park offers two guid­ed tours the Edi­acara Expe­ri­ence Tour (2‑hours) and the Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour (3‑hours) . We advise book­ing your tour well in advance of travel. Please note tours may be sub­ject to change, see book­ing page for cur­rent avail­able tours. We wel­come school or spe­cial inter­est groups book­ings, please con­tact us with your query Edi­acara Expe­ri­ence Tour (2‑hour experience) This tour includes: Ful­ly guid­ed tour from the Entrance Gate to the Vis­i­tor Precinct and back (in a wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus) Tour of the His­toric Woolshed Geo­log­i­cal Time­line walk Black­smith’s Shop AV Display Tours: Days & Times Mon­days, Wednes­days and Sat­ur­days – 1.30pm Prices (1 July 26 – 30 June 27) Adult: $88.00 Child: $52.50 Con­ces­sion: $70.50 Infant: No cost Com­pan­ion: No Cost Book your tour here. For large groups, those with time con­straints or young chil­dren this offers a great option with the oppor­tu­ni­ty to see and touch fos­sils in spe­cial­ly con­struct­ed fos­sil plinths at the Vis­i­tor Precinct with­out trav­el­ling out to the fos­sil field. Please note: This tour does not include a vis­it to the fos­sil field . Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour (3‑hour experience) Dive deep­er into the Edi­acaran peri­od on a 3‑hour guid­ed tour which includes: Ful­ly guid­ed tour from the Entrance Gate to the Vis­i­tor Precinct and Fos­sil Field and back (in a wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus) Tour of the His­toric Woolshed Geo­log­i­cal Time­line Walk Black­smith’s Shop AV Display Tour of the Fos­sil Field research site Tours: Days & Times Mon­days, Tues­days, Wednes­days, Fri­days and Sat­ur­days – 9.30am Addi­tion­al Tours (10 April – 15 October) Tues­days and Fri­days –1.30pm Prices (1 July 26 – 30 June 27) Adult: $176.00 Child: $105.00 Con­ces­sion: $141.00 Infant: No cost Com­pan­ion: No Cost Book your tour here. Know before you go: Meet at the park entrance (please arrive 15 min­utes pri­or to your tour time). Your guide will trans­port you by wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus into the park to the Vis­i­tor Precinct, point­ing out areas of interest. On the dri­ve through the park, you’ll expe­ri­ence the unique beau­ty of this spec­tac­u­lar loca­tion. A land of extreme con­trasts – both ​ ‘ hard and soft’ — rugged and harsh and yet serene and cap­ti­vat­ing. The spec­tac­u­lar land­scape fea­tures vast open spaces and gen­tle rolling hills with red and orange rock hues con­trast­ing against deep blue skies. Edu­ca­tion and Spe­cial Inter­est Groups Nilpe­na is able to offer some­thing tru­ly unique, an out­door class­room at an active fos­sil research site. There is a clear edu­ca­tion­al fit with geol­o­gy, deep time, evo­lu­tion and the fos­sil record as part of the greater Flinders Ranges. Our skilled guides can tai­lor tours to suit school groups or spe­cial inter­est groups. Con­tact us via email for enquiries DEW .​NilpenaEdiacaraNP@​sa.​gov.​au . Contact details Please note there is lim­it­ed phone cov­er­age in and around Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park. Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park — Park man­age­ment Con­tact us for gen­er­al or group book­ing enquiries Email: DEW .​NilpenaEdiacaraNP@​sa.​gov.​au Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park – After-hours duty offi­cer Phone: 0408 378 284 Port Augus­ta Nation­al Parks Wildlife Ser­vice South Aus­tralia Office Phone: (+61 8) 8648 5300 Email: dew.​flindersandoutback@​sa.​gov.​au Media enquiries Depart­ment for Envi­ron­ment and Water’s media contacts. Getting there Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is locat­ed in the Flinders Ranges and Out­back region of South Aus­tralia, approx­i­mate­ly 511km north of Adelaide. The park entrance is via the Out­back High­way, 115km north of Hawk­er or 41km south of Leigh Creek. View map to gate entrance. Entry to the park is only by guid­ed tour, at des­ig­nat­ed times. On arrival at the park entrance gate , you will board a wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus to con­tin­ue to the Vis­i­tor Precinct. Accessibility The infor­ma­tion below describes the ter­rain, trails, facil­i­ties and sup­port avail­able so you can make an informed choice about vis­it­ing Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park. Nilpe­na meets the Aus­tralian Stan­dards for Acces­si­bil­i­ty and is clas­si­fied an Acces­si­ble Park. Spe­cial Requirements When book­ing your tour let us know if you have any access or spe­cial require­ments. Tours are capped at 15 vis­i­tors, and our skilled guides will work to accom­mo­date vis­i­tors needs. Acces­si­ble Bus Nation­al parks have wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus with a lifter to enable those that use wheel­chairs or walk­ers to be able to board the bus. Toi­lets At the Black­smith Shop, there is one acces­si­ble toi­let, right hand trans­fer. In the main toi­let build­ing there is one acces­si­ble toi­let left hand transfer. Trans­fer from Park Entrance to Vis­i­tor Precinct The dri­ve into the Vis­i­tor Precinct takes about 10 min­utes (14km) and, depend­ing on the require­ments of the group, the tour gen­er­al­ly begins at the for­mer Woolshed. Wool­shed The inte­ri­or fea­tures a con­crete floor, and wheel­chair access is avail­able in the front sec­tion only. Vis­i­tor Precinct Trails From the Wool­shed, vis­i­tors pro­ceed along the Dawn of Life Time­line trail to the Black­smith Shop. This trail is rel­a­tive­ly flat and con­sists of com­pact­ed gravel. Black­smith Shop The Black­smith Shop hous­es the fos­sil bed known as Alice’s Restau­rant Bed . The fos­sil bed is dis­played on a pur­pose-built table designed to be acces­si­ble to a wide range of vis­i­tors, includ­ing those who use wheel­chairs. Vis­i­tors will be tak­en on a jour­ney immers­ing them­selves in an Edi­acaran fos­sil expe­ri­ence with the use of light­ing and cut­ting-edge audio-visu­al tech­nol­o­gy. Please note that light­ing con­di­tions will change through­out the audio­vi­su­al expe­ri­ence, which may affect indi­vid­u­als with light-relat­ed sen­so­ry sen­si­tiv­i­ties. The door can be left open to allow nat­ur­al light to come in if necessary. Fos­sil Field Transfer For vis­i­tors head­ing to the Fos­sil Field, it is approx­i­mate­ly a 10-minute dri­ve from the Vis­i­tor Precinct. The dri­ve to the fos­sil field involves uneven ter­rain, includ­ing a creek bed cross­ing which may result in a mod­er­ate­ly bumpy journey. Fos­sil Field Trail At the Fos­sil Field, vis­i­tors will fol­low a trail con­sist­ing of com­pact­ed grav­el, with sec­tions of large, flat boul­ders (designed to assist with drainage and min­imise ero­sion to the fos­sil field site). For those using a man­u­al wheel­chair, the use of a free­wheel attach­ment is recommended. The trail extends approx­i­mate­ly 500 metres return. The pri­ma­ry fos­sil bed is accessed via a set of stairs. Guides are able to tai­lor the expe­ri­ence to accom­mo­date vis­i­tors with mobil­i­ty require­ments and pro­vide a com­fort­able and inclu­sive vis­it. Please nom­i­nate your require­ments when book­ing to ensure the team can deliv­er a great experience. Access­ing Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park When to visit Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is open 16 March to 30 Novem­ber each year. Mild tem­per­a­tures from April to Octo­ber make this peri­od the most com­fort­able for vis­it­ing the Flinders Ranges region. Teach and Learn Resources for students Edicara activ­i­ty book The Edi­acara activ­i­ty book is a great resource and fun way for young school chil­dren to learn about fos­sils and the dis­cov­er­ies at Nilpena. Pro­duced by the Depart­ment for Envi­ron­ment and Water. Fos­sil Rock YouTube series Fos­sil Rock is a free, fun-filled YouTube series that brings sci­ence to life with catchy songs and excit­ing adven­tures for kids and fam­i­lies. Filmed at our very own Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park in South Australia’s Flinders Ranges, it’s packed with music, learn­ing, and the fas­ci­nat­ing sto­ry of the world’s old­est fos­sils. Aligned with the Aus­tralian Cur­ricu­lum across Sci­ence, HASS , Eng­lish, and Per­form­ing Arts, Fos­sil Rock is also a ready-made class­room resource. Teach­ers can access activ­i­ty sheets and cur­ricu­lum guides to inspire curios­i­ty in their students. Host­ed by children’s per­former Lucy Rasheed and guid­ed by palaeon­tol­o­gist Pro­fes­sor Mary Dros­er, Fos­sil Rock turns com­plex sci­en­tif­ic ideas into unfor­get­table songs and stories. Pro­duced by Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foundation. Explore the Edi­acara Bio­ta in an inter­ac­tive environment The Edi­acara Bio­ta edu­ca­tion­al web­site brings the world’s ear­li­est com­plex life to life in a fun, inter­ac­tive way. Explore ani­mat­ed seafloor scenes, 3D mod­els of key Edi­acaran organ­isms, and the pio­neer­ing dis­cov­er­ies made at Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park. Designed for stu­dents and the broad­er com­mu­ni­ty, it’s an easy-to-use, visu­al­ly rich resource that com­ple­ments the on-site expe­ri­ence and helps peo­ple every­where dis­cov­er South Australia’s ancient geo­log­i­cal story. Pro­duced by Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foundation Resources for teachers Edi­acaran Fos­sils of the Flinders Ranges ebook The Edi­acaran Fos­sils of the Flinders Ranges ebook , is an excel­lent teach­ing resource for upper pri­ma­ry and high school children. Pro­duced by the South Aus­tralian Depart­ment for Education Year 8 Edi­acaran Unit Sup­port­ing teach­ing of Year 8 Earth and Space Science. Pro­duced by Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foundation. David Attenborough’s First Life is avail­able on ABC iview, Episode 1 Arrival, 5 Novem­ber 2010. Refer from 32:40. Pets not allowed Dogs are not per­mit­ted in this park. Dis­cov­er which parks you can walk your dog by using our find a park tool , or read our blog, 17 dog-friend­ly walks in Ade­laide Parks , for inspiration. Assistance dogs Assis­tance dogs are per­mit­ted in most pub­lic places and are there­fore wel­come in South Australia’s parks and reserves. Assis­tance dogs must be appro­pri­ate­ly restrained on a lead and remain under your effec­tive con­trol at all times while in a park or reserve. As per the dogs in parks and reserves pol­i­cy, if the dog is not an accred­it­ed assis­tance dog, they must be trained to assist a per­son with a dis­abil­i­ty to alle­vi­ate that dis­abil­i­ty and meet stan­dards of hygiene and behav­iour appro­pri­ate for a dog in a pub­lic place. How­ev­er, refusal may be giv­en if the per­son with the dis­abil­i­ty is unable to pro­duce evi­dence the dog is an assis­tance dog with the appro­pri­ate training. Before tak­ing your assis­tance dog into a park that does not nor­mal­ly allow dogs, it is high­ly rec­om­mend­ed that you con­tact us so we can pro­vide you with the lat­est infor­ma­tion on any poten­tial haz­ards with­in spe­cif­ic parks that may affect your dog. Please con­tact the park via the con­tact details pro­vid­ed under the con­tact tab or con­tact the vis­i­tor ser­vice cen­tre via email or on Face­book . Facilities There are acces­si­ble toi­lets. Please bring plen­ty of drink­ing water for the dura­tion of your vis­it. Food and drinks are not avail­able for purchase. Traditional owners The Adnya­math­anha peo­ple (mean­ing rock peo­ple) are the Tra­di­tion­al Own­ers of the Flinders Ranges. Their con­nec­tion with the land stretch­es back many thou­sands of years. We encour­age you to find out more about the Adnya­math­anha cul­tur­al con­nec­tion to coun­try and to be respect­ful and respon­si­ble travellers. The Ikara-Flinders Ranges Nation­al Park Co-Man­age­ment Board pro­vides an advi­so­ry role to Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park. History Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is locat­ed on the tra­di­tion­al lands of the Adnya­math­anha peo­ple (mean­ing rock peo­ple). The Tra­di­tion­al Own­ers of this land trad­ed and con­duct­ed impor­tant cer­e­monies and camped along­side the per­ma­nent springs which still exist at Nilpe­na today. Pas­toral In the 1980s, Ross Fargher lease­hold­er of Nilpe­na Pas­toral Sta­tion, found Edi­acaran fos­sils on his recent­ly-acquired prop­er­ty when a fam­i­ly friend noticed rip­ple rocks of the ancient sea floor used as the floor­ing of Nilpena’s Woolshed. Sci­en­tif­ic Discovery In 2016, Nilpena’s most superbly pre­served beds, now known as Alice’s Restau­rant Bed , was unearthed by lead­ing palaeon­tol­o­gist Pro­fes­sor Mary Dros­er and her team from the Uni­ver­si­ty of Cal­i­for­nia River­side. The bed con­tains many rare species, with evi­dence depict­ing the seafloor was once a habi­tat and com­plex envi­ron­ment, where there was activ­i­ty of mobil­i­ty, feed­ing and reproduction. The fos­sil bed got its name in ref­er­ence to the US singer/​songwriter Arlo Guthrie who, in his song Alice’s Restau­rant (1967), sang ​ ‘ You can get any­thing you want at Alice’s Restau­rant …’ – just like the restau­rant there is plen­ty on offer with an amaz­ing diver­si­ty of fos­sils to be found. Renowned geol­o­gist late Reg Sprigg AO first dis­cov­ered fos­sils in the Edi­acara Hills, at the north­ern end of the Nation­al Park, in 1946. The Edi­acaran geo­log­i­cal peri­od was sub­se­quent­ly named after the dis­cov­ery loca­tion, and the fos­sil Sprig­gi­na was named in his hon­our. Sprig­gi­na lat­er became South Aus­trali­a’s fos­sil emblem. To date, more than 47 fos­sil species have been record­ed at Nilpena. Sig­nif­i­cance Nilpe­na was placed on Australia’s Nation­al Her­itage List in 2007 for its qual­i­ty of intact fos­sil specimens. The World Her­itage bid for the Flinders Ranges com­pos­es sev­en sites (includ­ing Nilpe­na) with geo­log­i­cal and palaeon­to­log­i­cal sig­nif­i­cance. A deci­sion on World Her­itage sta­tus is expect­ed in mid-2027. Nilpe­na con­tains new­ly described taxa, includ­ing one named after Sir David Atten­bor­ough (Atten­bori­ties janeae) who vis­it­ed Nilpe­na to film part of the BBC Doc­u­men­tary ​ ‘ First Life’ and anoth­er after Pres­i­dent Barack Oba­ma (Oba­mus coro­na­tus) for his com­mit­ment to sci­en­tif­ic research. Edi­acaran fos­sil site — Nilpe­na Sta­tion, South Australia Creation of Nilpena Ediacara National Park The cre­ation and estab­lish­ment of Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park was realised through South Aus­tralian Gov­ern­ment fund­ing and Com­mon­wealth Gov­ern­ment grants, in part­ner­ship with the Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foun­da­tion , Wyss Foun­da­tion Cam­paign for Nature , and Foun­da­tion for Nation­al Parks and Wildlife. Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park was cre­at­ed in 2021 and offi­cial­ly opened 27 April 2023. Flinders Ranges Ediacara Foundation Found­ed in 2018, the Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foun­da­tion exists to con­serve the Edi­acara fos­sils of the Flinders Ranges in per­pe­tu­ity, and to ensure the world ben­e­fits from the knowl­edge they embody. The Foun­da­tion achieves its pur­pose through in situ con­ser­va­tion, and sup­port­ing edu­ca­tion and tourism, mak­ing the fos­sils and their sig­nif­i­cance acces­si­ble for all. Learn more about the Flinders Ranges Edi­acara Foundation. Flinders Ranges Explore oth­er parks in the Flinders Ranges Ikara-Flinders Ranges Nation­al park Vulkathun­ha-Gam­mon Ranges Nation­al Park Learn more about the Flinders Ranges and Out­back region . World Heritage for the Flinders Ranges World Her­itage List­ing for the Flinders Ranges is being pur­sued for its geo­log­i­cal and palaeon­to­log­i­cal sig­nif­i­cance. The pro­posed nom­i­na­tion is focused on some of the world’s most out­stand­ing and acces­si­ble fos­sil records, includ­ing those at Nilpe­na, that evi­dence how com­plex ani­mal life evolved on our planet. Like nowhere else on Earth, the fos­sil evi­dence found at Nilpe­na takes us to the dawn of ani­mal life – the Edi­acaran bio­ta – and the emer­gence of thriv­ing eco­log­i­cal com­mu­ni­ties. The sea floor cap­tured at Nilpe­na is a place of firsts: the ear­li­est ani­mals, and eco­log­i­cal inno­va­tions such as the advent of mobil­i­ty, of scav­eng­ing, and of sex­u­al reproduction. The com­plet­ed nom­i­na­tion was sub­mit­ted to the UNESCO World Her­itage Cen­tre in Paris in Jan­u­ary 2026. After a fur­ther assess­ment process, a final deci­sion on World Her­itage sta­tus is expect­ed in mid-2027. Learn more about the Flinders Ranges World Her­itage bid. For large groups, those with time con­straints or young chil­dren this offers a great option with the oppor­tu­ni­ty to see and touch fos­sils in spe­cial­ly con­struct­ed fos­sil plinths at the Vis­i­tor Precinct with­out trav­el­ling out to the fos­sil field. Please note: This tour does not include a vis­it to the fos­sil field . Fos­sil Field Explo­ration Tour (3‑hour experience) Dive deep­er into the Edi­acaran peri­od on a 3‑hour guid­ed tour which includes: Ful­ly guid­ed tour from the Entrance Gate to the Vis­i­tor Precinct and Fos­sil Field and back (in a wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus) Tour of the His­toric Woolshed Geo­log­i­cal Time­line Walk Black­smith’s Shop AV Display Tour of the Fos­sil Field research site Tours: Days & Times Mon­days, Tues­days, Wednes­days, Fri­days and Sat­ur­days – 9.30am Addi­tion­al Tours (10 April – 15 October) Tues­days and Fri­days –1.30pm Prices (1 July 26 – 30 June 27) Adult: $176.00 Child: $105.00 Con­ces­sion: $141.00 Infant: No cost Com­pan­ion: No Cost Book your tour here. Know before you go: Meet at the park entrance (please arrive 15 min­utes pri­or to your tour time). Your guide will trans­port you by wheel­chair acces­si­ble bus into the park to the Vis­i­tor Precinct, point­ing out areas of interest. On the dri­ve through the park, you’ll expe­ri­ence the unique beau­ty of this spec­tac­u­lar loca­tion. A land of extreme con­trasts – both ​ ‘ hard and soft’ — rugged and harsh and yet serene and cap­ti­vat­ing. The spec­tac­u­lar land­scape fea­tures vast open spaces and gen­tle rolling hills with red and orange rock hues con­trast­ing against deep blue skies. Edu­ca­tion and Spe­cial Inter­est Groups Nilpe­na is able to offer some­thing tru­ly unique, an out­door class­room at an active fos­sil research site. There is a clear edu­ca­tion­al fit with geol­o­gy, deep time, evo­lu­tion and the fos­sil record as part of the greater Flinders Ranges. Our skilled guides can tai­lor tours to suit school groups or spe­cial inter­est groups. Con­tact us via email for enquiries DEW .​NilpenaEdiacaraNP@​sa.​gov.​au . Water Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is with­in a remote, rugged area. Please bring plen­ty of drink­ing water for the dura­tion of your visit. Know before you go Access to Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park is restrict­ed to guid­ed tours only. The park is remote and dry, so pro­tec­tive cloth­ing is required for both warm and cool conditions. Fire This park is closed on days of Cat­a­stroph­ic Fire Dan­ger and may also be closed on days of Extreme Fire Danger. You can deter­mine the cur­rent fire dan­ger rat­ing by check­ing the Fire Ban Dis­trict map on the CFS web­site or call the CFS Bush­fire Infor­ma­tion Hot­line 1800 362 361. Entry fees Entry to this park is by guid­ed tour only. The Edi­acara Expe­ri­ence Tour is from $80 per person. Park pass This park is not part of the park pass system. Which parks are includ­ed in the park pass system? Camping and accommodation No camp­ing or accom­mo­da­tion is avail­able with­in this park. A num­ber of overnight options exist in near­by Ikara-Flinders Ranges Nation­al Park and sur­round­ing Flinders Ranges towns and sta­tion stays. Park maps Nilpe­na Edi­acara Nation­al Park Maps on your mobile If you have a smart­phone or tablet you can down­load the free Aven­za PDF Map app and have inter­ac­tive nation­al park maps on hand when you need them. The app uses your device’s built-in GPS to plot your real-time loca­tion with­in the park onto a map. The app can be used with­out a net­work con­nec­tion and with­out roam­ing charges. You can also mea­sure area and dis­tance, plot pho­tos and drop place­mark pins. How to get it work­ing on your device: 1. Down­load the Aven­za PDF maps app from the app store whilst you are still in range (its free!). 2. Open up the app and click the shop­ping cart icon. 3. Click ​ ‘ Find’ and type the name of the nation­al park or reserve you are look­ing for. 4. Click on the map you are after and install it (all our maps are free). 5. You will now find a list of your installed maps on the home page of the Aven­za app. 6. Use our maps through the Aven­za PDF map app while in the park and nev­er take a wrong turn again. approved_stops.name: Nilpena Ediacara National Park
approved_stops.quote: Nilpena Ediacara National Park, which includes the former Ediacara Conservation Park, is a national park located in the northern Flinders Ranges, in the state of South Australia. It is significant for its abundance of Ediacaran fossils, so named because of their discovery in the Ediacara Hills. It is located about around 551 km (342 mi) north of the city of Adelaide, around 30 kilometres (19 miles) south-west of the town of Leigh Creek in the state's Far North, and lies on the traditional lands of the Adnyamathanha people.
